sourceEnglishTitle: Saying No: Unsafe Request from the Homeowner
sourceEnglishObjective: Refuse an unsafe or improper request from a homeowner politely and firmly, and offer a safe alternative
sourceEnglishSpeaking: You are the crew lead and the AI is a homeowner in a hurry who asks for something unsafe: refuse politely and firmly with no recomiendo que and no es posible que, explain the risk, and offer a safe alternative.
sourceSpanishReaderTitle: Not in Lightning, Not Without Underlayment

sourceGrammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que

examples.es: No suban al techo con relámpagos.
examples.en: Don't go up on the roof in lightning.

examples.es: No recomiendo que trabajemos con la superficie mojada.
examples.en: I don't recommend that we work on a wet surface.

example.target: No recomiendo que trabajemos con relámpagos.
example.native: I don't recommend that we work in lightning.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Subjunctive after no recomiendo que: trabajemos.

example.target: No suban hasta que yo diga.
example.native: Don't go up until I say so.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Negative command: no suban (ustedes), no subas (tú).

example.target: No dejen herramientas de metal en el techo.
example.native: Don't leave metal tools on the roof.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Negative command: no dejen (ustedes), no dejes (tú).

example.target: Aquí nunca nos saltamos la sub-capa.
example.native: Here we never skip the underlayment.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Subjunctive after no es posible que: nos saltemos.

example.target: Lo que sí podemos hacer es cubrir el techo con lona.
example.native: What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Stem change o to ue, except in the nosotros form: podemos.

candidateObjective: 家主からの危険または不適切な依頼を丁寧に断り、代案を伝える。
candidateFocus: お気持ちは分かりますが acknowledges the customer before refusal. ～ことはできません states the limit, and ～なら gives a conditional finish time.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 雷が発生している間の作業はお勧めしません。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: I don't recommend that we work in lightning.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 私が指示するまで屋根に上がらないでください。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Don't go up until I say so.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 金属工具を屋根に置いたままにしないでください。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Don't leave metal tools on the roof.

archivedForms.exampleJa: ここでは下葺き材を省きません。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Here we never skip the underlayment.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 代わりに屋根を防水シートで覆うことはできます。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp.

archivedSpeaking.opening: お急ぎなのは分かりますが、雷の中での作業や下葺き材を省くことはできません。屋根を防水シートで覆い、雷雨が過ぎたら再開します。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Respond to a homeowner who asks the crew to work during a storm and omit underlayment. Decline both requests politely and directly, explain why the crew will not do either, and offer the tarp-and-return alternative.

cards.reviewNote: Japanese 雷 can mean thunder or lightning; confirm the precise source lightning sense.
The source gloss conflates lightning strike and electric shock; preserve the physical hazard accurately.
Wet surface is a roof-access hazard in context; confirm precise Japanese trade wording.
Manufacturer-warranty condition requires an identified roofing product/system.

cards.sourceSpanish: No recomiendo que trabajemos con relámpagos.
cards.sourceEnglish: I don't recommend that we work in lightning.
cards.archivedJapanese: 雷が発生している間の作業はお勧めしません。
cards.archivedEnglish: I don't recommend that we work in lightning.
cards.reviewNote: Lightning-work refusal is a safety instruction requiring qualified source and trade review.

cards.sourceSpanish: No es posible que nos saltemos la sub-capa.
cards.sourceEnglish: It isn't possible for us to skip the underlayment.
cards.archivedJapanese: 下葺き材を省くことはできません。
cards.archivedEnglish: It isn't possible for us to skip the underlayment.
cards.reviewNote: Skipping underlayment and warranty consequences depend on the specified system.

cards.sourceSpanish: Entiendo su prisa, pero no puedo hacerlo.
cards.sourceEnglish: I understand your hurry, but I can't do it.
cards.candidateJapanese: お急ぎなのは分かりますが、それはできません。
cards.archivedJapanese: お急ぎなのは分かりますが、それはできません。
cards.archivedEnglish: I understand your hurry, but I can't do it.

cards.sourceSpanish: Lamentablemente, eso no lo podemos hacer.
cards.sourceEnglish: Unfortunately, that's something we can't do.
cards.candidateJapanese: 申し訳ありませんが、それはできません。
cards.archivedJapanese: 申し訳ありませんが、それはできません。
cards.archivedEnglish: Unfortunately, that's something we can't do.

cards.sourceSpanish: Lo que sí podemos hacer es cubrir el techo con lona.
cards.sourceEnglish: What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp.
cards.archivedJapanese: 屋根を防水シートで覆うことはできます。
cards.archivedEnglish: What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp.
cards.reviewNote: Temporary tarp work must not imply access during lightning or premature reentry.

cards.sourceSpanish: No suban hasta que yo diga.
cards.sourceEnglish: Don't go up until I say so.
cards.archivedJapanese: 私が指示するまで屋根に上がらないでください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Don't go up until I say so.
cards.reviewNote: Roof-access command needs a site-specific authorization and safe reentry decision.

cards.archivedJapanese: 誰のためにも危険を冒さないでください。
cards.reviewNote: Absolute safety command needs a qualified trade and register decision.

reader.sourceSpanish: Eran las dos de la tarde, y se escuchaba un trueno lejos, hacia el oeste.
reader.sourceEnglish: It was two in the afternoon, and thunder could be heard far off, to the west.
reader.candidateJapanese: 午後二時、西の遠くから雷鳴が聞こえました。
reader.archivedJapanese: 午後二時、西の遠くから雷鳴が聞こえました。
reader.archivedEnglish: It was two in the afternoon, and thunder could be heard far off, to the west.

reader.sourceSpanish: La señora Flores salió de la casa con prisa y habló con Rogelio.
reader.sourceEnglish: Mrs. Flores came out of the house in a hurry and spoke with Rogelio.
reader.candidateJapanese: フローレスさんは急いで家から出て、ロヘリオに話しかけました。
reader.archivedJapanese: フローレスさんは急いで家から出て、ロヘリオに話しかけました。
reader.archivedEnglish: Mrs. Flores came out of the house in a hurry and spoke with Rogelio.

reader.sourceSpanish: Señora Flores: Mis hijos llegan el sábado, así que quiero que sigan trabajando aunque llueva.
reader.sourceEnglish: Mrs. Flores: My children arrive on Saturday, so I want you to keep working even if it rains.
reader.candidateJapanese: フローレスさん「子どもたちが土曜日に来るので、雨が降っても作業を続けてください。」
reader.archivedJapanese: フローレスさん「子どもたちが土曜日に来るので、雨が降っても作業を続けてください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Mrs. Flores: My children arrive on Saturday, so I want you to keep working even if it rains.

reader.sourceSpanish: Señora Flores: Y para ahorrar, pongan las tejas sin la sub-capa.
reader.sourceEnglish: Mrs. Flores: And to save money, put the shingles on without the underlayment.
reader.archivedJapanese: フローレスさん「費用を節約するため、下葺き材なしでシングル材を敷いてください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Mrs. Flores: And to save money, put the shingles on without the underlayment.
reader.reviewNote: Homeowner requests omission of underlayment; preserve this as a refused request, not a recommendation.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Entiendo su prisa, pero no puedo hacerlo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: I understand your hurry, but I can't do it.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「お急ぎなのは分かりますが、それはできません。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「お急ぎなのは分かりますが、それはできません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: I understand your hurry, but I can't do it.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Con relámpagos, el techo es el peor lugar, y no recomiendo que trabajemos con relámpagos ni con la superficie mojada.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: In lightning, the roof is the worst place, and I don't recommend that we work in lightning or on a wet surface.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「雷が発生しているとき、屋根は最も危険な場所です。雷の中や濡れた表面での作業はお勧めしません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: In lightning, the roof is the worst place, and I don't recommend that we work in lightning or on a wet surface.
reader.reviewNote: Lightning and wet-roof work refusal is safety-critical; review source intensity and natural Japanese.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Una descarga eléctrica puede matar a una persona, y ese riesgo no lo voy a aceptar.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: A lightning strike can kill a person, and I'm not going to accept that risk.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「落雷による電撃は命に関わります。その危険は受け入れません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: A lightning strike can kill a person, and I'm not going to accept that risk.
reader.reviewNote: Lightning strike fatality and electric-shock wording need exact physical and clinical senses.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Sobre la sub-capa, lamentablemente, eso no lo podemos hacer.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: About the underlayment, unfortunately, that's something we can't do.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「下葺き材についても、申し訳ありませんが、それはできません。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「下葺き材についても、申し訳ありませんが、それはできません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: About the underlayment, unfortunately, that's something we can't do.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: No es posible que nos saltemos la sub-capa, porque el fabricante la pide para la garantía.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: It isn't possible for us to skip the underlayment, because the manufacturer requires it for the warranty.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「メーカーが保証の条件として求めているので、下葺き材を省くことはできません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: It isn't possible for us to skip the underlayment, because the manufacturer requires it for the warranty.
reader.reviewNote: Manufacturer warranty condition cannot be universal without a specified product/system.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Ese atajo parece un ahorro hoy, pero más adelante sería una gotera y un gasto mucho mayor.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: That shortcut looks like savings today, but later it would be a leak and a much bigger expense.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「この近道は今日の節約に見えても、後で雨漏りとさらに大きな出費につながります。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: That shortcut looks like savings today, but later it would be a leak and a much bigger expense.
reader.reviewNote: The source predicts a future leak and greater expense; review the categorical claim.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Lo que sí podemos hacer es cubrir el techo con lona y volver en cuanto pase la tormenta eléctrica.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp and come back as soon as the thunderstorm passes.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「代わりに屋根を防水シートで覆い、雷雨が過ぎたら戻ることができます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp and come back as soon as the thunderstorm passes.
reader.reviewNote: Tarp placement and return after the storm require a safe-access sequence not specified in source.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Así terminaríamos el viernes, si el pronóstico ayuda, y usted tendría su techo antes del sábado.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: That way we would finish on Friday, if the forecast helps, and you would have your roof before Saturday.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「予報が良ければ金曜日に仕上がり、土曜日までに屋根が完成します。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: That way we would finish on Friday, if the forecast helps, and you would have your roof before Saturday.
reader.reviewNote: Friday finish is conditional on forecast; archived Japanese must not guarantee the date.

reader.sourceSpanish: La señora Flores pensó un momento y aceptó la alternativa.
reader.sourceEnglish: Mrs. Flores thought for a moment and accepted the alternative.
reader.candidateJapanese: フローレスさんは少し考え、代案を受け入れました。
reader.archivedJapanese: フローレスさんは少し考え、代案を受け入れました。
reader.archivedEnglish: Mrs. Flores thought for a moment and accepted the alternative.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio habló con la cuadrilla: No suban hasta que yo diga, y no dejen herramientas de metal en el techo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio talked to the crew: Don't go up until I say so, and don't leave metal tools on the roof.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオは作業班に「私が指示するまで屋根に上がらず、金属工具を屋根に置いたままにしないでください」と伝えました。
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio talked to the crew: Don't go up until I say so, and don't leave metal tools on the roof.
reader.reviewNote: Do not leave metal tools on the roof, but retrieval timing and storm procedure are unspecified.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: La decisión es mía, y la responsabilidad también.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: The decision is mine, and so is the responsibility.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「判断するのは私です。責任も私が負います。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: The decision is mine, and so is the responsibility.
reader.reviewNote: The foreman claims personal responsibility; legal/contract authority varies by locale.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Kevin, no te arriesgues por nadie; la norma de seguridad es la misma para todos.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Kevin, don't take risks for anyone; the safety rule is the same for everyone.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「ケビン、誰のためにも危険を冒さないでください。安全規則は全員同じです。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Kevin, don't take risks for anyone; the safety rule is the same for everyone.
reader.reviewNote: Safety rule and command to Kevin require qualified jobsite register and authority review.

see.label: Identify the wet roof, lightning, underlayment, and tarp.

recall.label: Recall thunderstorm, manufacturer warranty, shortcut, and alternative.

hear.label: Distinguish 雷 from 雷鳴 when spoken.

type.label: Type 'It isn't possible for us to skip the underlayment' in Japanese.

say.label: Politely refuse the homeowner's request and offer the tarp alternative.

write.label: Write the crew instruction after the homeowner accepts the alternative.

curriculumAdaptationNote: The source portrays an unsafe homeowner request to keep working in rain and omit underlayment. Preserve Rogelio’s refusal and the order of lightning/wet-roof risk, warranty explanation, proposed tarp after the storm and conditional Friday finish. Do not present the tarp, metal-tool instruction, reentry timing, manufacturer warranty or personal liability as universal jobsite directions without an identified system and qualified safety/product/contract review. The lightning-strike card conflates electrical injury and strike terminology. Grammar and Spanish verbs are pinned separately. No selected learner/audio text or progress identity is created.
